B_access_pricing.mcp_access_cost_details: The reviewed Productivity MCP documentation does not state a separate MCP fee or a specific Productivity MCP charge. Algolia’s overview says Public MCP usage counts toward the existing Algolia plan and has no separate MCP fee; that statement is for Public MCP, not clearly for this endpoint.
B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: Algolia pricing lists a Free plan and paid plans including Grow, Grow Plus, and Elevate; exact prices and usage vary by plan and configuration.
B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: The linked Algolia service has plan and usage-based limits. Productivity MCP-specific per-call charges, quotas, or rates were not found in the reviewed official documentation.
B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: An account owner enables Productivity MCP in the Algolia dashboard. Each user authenticates separately; access follows that user’s Algolia permissions across applications. Analytics tools require Analytics permission and recommendations require the Recommend feature according to the companion skill.
B_access_pricing.restrictions_controlled_by: Algolia account administrator enables the feature; Algolia controls OAuth and server behavior; user’s Algolia permissions control accessible data.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. The official guide calls Productivity MCP read-only and says it cannot create, update, or delete indices, records, or settings. Tool annotations (readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint, openWorldHint) are not published. 2. No server-enforced confirmation, approval, or elicitation workflow is documented; there are no documented write tools. 3. OAuth uses the public scope. Algolia states that each user signs in separately and that their Algolia permissions determine access; the feature must be enabled for the account. Client allowlists, redirect URI approval policy, token lifetime, and admin role details are not stated. 4. No read-only URL mode, toolset filter, environment selector, or regional Productivity endpoint is documented. Productivity MCP scopes across the account’s applications, not individual applications. 5. No MCP-specific masking or field exclusions are documented. Official guidance says data accessible to the user is available to the MCP and prompts and outputs should be treated as internal data. 6. Productivity-specific quotas, rate limits, bulk caps, output truncation, and per-call costs were not found. Algolia’s general plan limits and usage charges may apply to the linked software; the reviewed documentation does not specify how this endpoint is billed. 7. Public server implementation is unavailable, so parameter validation, coercion, and overrides are unknown. The companion skill says applicationId is an enum and tells agents to use exact case-sensitive index names. 8. MCP-specific logs, audit trails, telemetry, and opt-out controls were not found. 9. The documented tools and descriptions include no feedback, rating, survey, report, or upsell action. 10. Algolia distributes an algolia-mcp companion skill outside the server. Its workflow guidance is not shown as server-enforced. 11. No persistent agent memory or state-dependent tool availability is documented. 12. The endpoint presents a Productivity MCP tool list; no hierarchical or proxied sub-server structure is documented. Algolia documents separate Public and DevEx MCP offerings. 13. No raw API request, arbitrary SQL, script execution, or general-purpose escape hatch tool appears in the official Productivity MCP tool list.

D_server_side_logic.server_structure_explanation: The documented Productivity MCP is presented as one hosted endpoint with a tool list. Other Algolia MCP products have different endpoints and purposes; they are separate offerings.

E_aggregated.action_count_comment: The official Productivity MCP guide lists 16 core tools and two additional ChatGPT compatibility tools, search and fetch, for 18 documented names total. No official numeric total is stated. Manufact reports 16 tools and names 12 analytics tools in its list; it does not include the two ChatGPT compatibility tools in that count. Other reviewed catalogues either do not publish a complete native tool list or report the remote Productivity MCP inventory as unestablished. No catalogue-only tools were added. Parameters and annotations are not published in the official tool table.

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: Algolia’s guide recommends exploring and validating index data before making changes elsewhere and recommends treating prompts and outputs as internal data. These are client-facing instructions; no enforcement mechanism is documented beyond the read-only tool surface.
F_documentation.governance_promises: Algolia states the Productivity MCP is read-only and inherits the signed-in user’s Algolia permissions. Product-specific terms state that an MCP server acts “solely as a passive connector” and that returned Subscriber Data is transmitted “at Subscriber’s direction.” The terms also include a NeuralSearch training license for eligible plans and data, with Personal Data excluded and dashboard opt-out; that provision is not stated as an MCP-specific processing rule.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: Algolia describes the Productivity MCP as user-scoped access for internal workflows and says users can explore and analyze applications and indices permitted by their Algolia permissions.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: The read-only restriction is described as a product capability, but public server code is unavailable, so its implementation cannot be independently checked. Permission inheritance is documented, but no detailed OAuth-to-role mapping is public. Internal-data handling is guidance to users, not a described server-side masking or retention control. Product-specific terms establish general MCP and NeuralSearch terms but do not detail MCP-specific logging, retention, or telemetry.

contradictions: The official Productivity MCP guide names 16 core tools and then lists two additional ChatGPT compatibility tools (search and fetch), while Manufact reports 16 MCP tools. The mismatch appears to concern the two compatibility tools; the guide does not state an overall total.

The endpoint’s protected-resource metadata advertises scopes_supported ["public"], while Algolia documentation describes user-specific permission inheritance. The metadata scope name alone does not explain the permission mapping.
observations_for_research: Algolia distinguishes user-scoped Productivity MCP from application-scoped Public MCP and code-snippet-focused DevEx MCP; their access models and endpoints differ.
The official guide’s two ChatGPT compatibility tool names expand its documented action inventory beyond the 16 core Productivity MCP tools.
notes: Reviewed the prepared links.json, links_check.txt, pages/INDEX.txt, all captured official documentation and catalogue pages, OAuth responses supplied with the task, and the local Algolia skills repository. The repository is a companion skills distribution, not the hosted server implementation; its tool-selection and workflow guidance is useful provenance but does not establish server handlers or schemas. Official guide has names and short purposes but no tool schemas, annotations, complete result formats, or initialize instructions. Manufact’s report of 16 tools is third-party evidence and was checked against the official tool table. No unofficial server evidence was used for actions.
